questions.problem: Given an arithmetic sequence that has ${a}_{10}=23$ and the common difference $d=3$, what is the general formula for the $n$th term of the sequence?
questions.worked_solution:
Since ${a}_{10}=23$ is $9$ jumps after ${a}_{1},$ we can determine the first term of the sequence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{10} & ={a}_{1}+9d \\ 23 & ={a}_{1}+9(3) \\ 23 & ={a}_{1}+27 \\ -4 & ={a}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the formula for the $n$th term is:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}+(n-1)d \\  & =-4+(n-1)(3) \\  & =-4+3n-3 \\  & =3n-7\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the general formula for the $n$th term of the arithmetic sequence that begins with 

$$
19,\,17,\,15,\,…
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The formula for the $n$th term of an arithmetic sequence (in function notation) is

$$
f(n)=f(1)+(n-1)d.
$$

From the first few terms

$$
19,\,17,\,15,\,…
$$

we see that the first term is $f(1)=19$ and the common difference is 

$$
d=17-19=-2.
$$

So, we substitute into the formula and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(n) & =f(1)+(n-1)d \\  & =19+(n-1)(-2) \\  & =19-2n+2 \\  & =21-2n\end{aligned}
$$

    

Therefore, the formula for the $n$th term is $f(n)=21-2n.$

questions.problem:
Find the $33$rd term of the following arithmetic sequence.

$$
13,\,8,\,3,\,-2,\,…
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The formula for the $n$th term of an arithmetic sequence is

$$
{a}_{n}={a}_{1}+(n-1)d.
$$

First, we will write the formula for the $n$th term of this sequence. From the first few terms

$$
13,\,8,\,3,\,-2,\,…
$$

we see that the first term is ${a}_{1}=13$ and the common difference is 

$$
d=8-13=-5.
$$

So, we substitute into the formula and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}+(n-1)d \\  & =13+(n-1)(-5) \\  & =13-5n+5 \\  & =18-5n\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use our formula to find the $33$rd term. All we have to do is substitute $n=33:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =18-5n \\ {a}_{33} & =18-5(33) \\  & =18-165 \\  & =-147\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $33$rd term of the sequence is ${a}_{33}=-147.$

Find the formula for the $n$th term of an arithmetic sequence if the first term is $-2$ and the second term is $3.$

$$
f(n)=f(1)+(n-1)d.
$$

We are given the first term $f(1)=-2.$ Also, the common difference of the sequence can be found as

$$
d=3-(-2)=5.
$$

So, we substitute into the formula and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(n) & =f(1)+(n-1)d \\  & =-2+(n-1)(5) \\  & =-2+5n-5 \\  & =5n-7\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the following arithmetic sequence.

$$
-17,\,-12,\,-7,\,-2,\,…
$$

What is the $24$th term of this sequence?

${a}_{24}=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
The formula for the $n$th term of an arithmetic sequence is

$$
{a}_{n}={a}_{1}+(n-1)d.
$$

First, we will write the formula for the $n$th term of this sequence. From the first few terms

$$
-17,\,-12,\,-7,\,-2,\,…,
$$

we see that the first term is ${a}_{1}=-17$ and the common difference is 

$$
d=-12-(-17)=5.
$$

So, we substitute into the formula and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}+(n-1)d \\  & =-17+(n-1)(5) \\  & =-17+5n-5 \\  & =5n-22\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use our formula to find the $24$th term. All we have to do is substitute $n=24:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =5n-22 \\ {a}_{24} & =5(24)-22 \\  & =120-22 \\  & =98\end{aligned}
$$
